correctness.rationale: The archival scroll formula gives \(D_k=kd-nk(k-1)\) for every \(1\le k\le d_1\). Since \(k(k-1)\) is always even, \(\gcd(d,2n)\) divides every \(D_k\). Because \(d_1\ge2\), the first two terms are \(D_1=d\) and \(D_2=2d-2n\), whose gcd is exactly \(\gcd(d,2n)\). Thus the whole-tower gcd equality is exact. The embedded checker independently verifies the arithmetic identity over a broad finite grid.

value.rationale: Higher-dual degrees measure successive orders of osculating hyperplane contact and form a natural geometric tower. The theorem determines the exact common prime content of that entire tower and shows that it depends only on total degree and dimension, not on the splitting type. It gives an immediate and complete primitivity criterion and prime-wise divisibility law for every scroll in the stable osculating range.
